resp.query: When can bail earlier granted under IPC be cancelled if serious charges like UA(P)A are added, as in Jibangshu Paul vs NIA?
resp.answer: Based on the case of Jibangshu Paul vs National Investigation Agency provided in the context, when serious new charges under special laws like the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UA(P)A) are added to an existing case where bail was earlier granted under IPC sections, the earlier bail does not automatically extend to the new charges. The Gauhati High Court held that newly added serious UA(P) Act offences require separate consideration, and the Special Judge cannot continue prior bail orders granted solely under IPC sections. Consequently, fresh bail is required, and custody may be ordered.

resp.query: What remedies does a homebuyer have under Section 18 of RERA 2016 if the builder delays flat possession?

Under **The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016**, **Section 18: Return of amount and compensation for delay in possession**, the law provides that: If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment, plot or building in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale or duly completed by the date specified therein, the promoter shall be liable on demand to the allottees, in case the allottee wishes to withdraw from the project, to return the amount received by him in respect of that apartment, plot, building, with interest at such rate as may be prescribed in this behalf including compensation. If the allottee does not intend to withdraw from the project, he shall be paid, by the promoter, interest for every month of delay, till the handing over of t...
